$\displaystyle=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{2n}}I(A:B|M)_{\hat{\sigma}_{ABM|Z=\mathbf{z}}}\,\mathrm{d}p_{Z}(\mathbf{z})$
$\displaystyle=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{2n}}I(A:B|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{ABM}}\,\mathrm{d}p_{Z}(\mathbf{z})=0\;.$
(77)
We then have from the data-processing inequality for the quantum mutual information
$\displaystyle I(C:Z|M)_{\hat{\sigma}_{CMZ}}$
$\displaystyle\leq I(AB:Z|M)_{\hat{\sigma}_{ABMZ}}$
$\displaystyle=I(A:Z|M)_{\hat{\sigma}_{AMZ}}+I(B:Z|M)_{\hat{\sigma}_{BMZ}}$
$\displaystyle\phantom{=}+I(A:B|MZ)_{\hat{\sigma}_{ABMZ}}-I(A:B|M)_{\hat{\sigma}_{ABM}}$
$\displaystyle\leq I(A:Z|M)_{\hat{\sigma}_{AMZ}}+I(B:Z|M)_{\hat{\sigma}_{BMZ}}\;.$
(78)
Proceeding as in the proof of Theorem 3.1 we get
$I(A:Z|M)_{\hat{\sigma}_{AMZ}(t)}=S(A|M)_{\hat{\sigma}_{AM}(t)}-S(A|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{AM}}\;,$
(79)
where
$\displaystyle\hat{\sigma}_{AM}(t)$
$\displaystyle=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{2n}}\hat{D}_{A}\left(\frac{\lambda\,\mathbf{z}}{\sqrt{\eta}}\right)\,\hat{\rho}_{AM}\,{\hat{D}_{A}\left(\frac{\lambda\,\mathbf{z}}{\sqrt{\eta}}\right)}^{\dagger}\,\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{|\mathbf{z}|^{2}}{2t}}\frac{\mathrm{d}^{2n}z}{(2\pi\,t)^{n}}$
$\displaystyle=\left(\mathcal{N}_{A}\left(\frac{\lambda^{2}\,t}{\eta}\right)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M}\right)(\hat{\rho}_{AM})\;,$
(80)
hence
$I(A:Z|M)_{\hat{\sigma}_{AMZ}(t)}=\Delta_{A|M}(\hat{\rho}_{AM})\left(\frac{\lambda^{2}\,t}{\eta}\right)\;.$
(81)
We can analogously show that
$I(B:Z|M)_{\hat{\sigma}_{BMZ}(t)}=\Delta_{B|M}(\hat{\rho}_{BM})\left(\frac{(1-\lambda)^{2}\,t}{|1-\eta|}\right)\;,$
(82)
and (78) becomes the claim (69).
5 Universal asymptotic scaling of quantum conditional entropy
In this Section, we prove that the quantum conditional entropy has a universal asymptotic scaling in the infinite-time limit under the heat semigroup evolution (Theorem 5.2).
The proof is based on the following more general result, that provides a new universal lower bound for the conditional entropy of the output of any quantum Gaussian channel.
Theorem 5.1 (universal lower bound for quantum conditional entropy)
Let  $A$ ,  $B$  be quantum Gaussian systems with  $m$  and  $n$  modes, respectively, and  $\Phi:A\to B$  a quantum Gaussian channel.
Let  $\hat{\rho}_{AM}$  be a quantum state on  $AM$  such that
$\mathrm{Tr}_{A}\left[\hat{H}_{A}\,\hat{\rho}_{A}\right]<\infty\;,\qquad S(\hat{\rho}_{M})<\infty\;.$
(83)
Then, for any quantum system  $M$  and any joint quantum state  $\hat{\rho}_{AM}$
$S(B|M)_{(\Phi\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})}\geq\lim_{\nu\to\infty}S(B|A^{\prime})_{(\Phi\otimes\mathbb{I}_{A^{\prime}})(\hat{\omega}_{AA^{\prime}}(\nu))}\;,$
(84)
where  $A^{\prime}$  is a Gaussian quantum system with  $m$  modes, and for any  $\nu\geq\frac{1}{2}$ ,  $\hat{\omega}_{AA^{\prime}}(\nu)$  is a purification of the thermal Gaussian state  $\hat{\omega}_{A}(\nu)$  on  $A$  with covariance matrix  $\nu\,I_{2m}$ .
Proof
Since the quantum conditional entropy is concave, we can restrict to  $\hat{\rho}_{AM}$  pure.
Let  $K:\mathbb{R}^{2m}\to\mathbb{R}^{2n}$  be the matrix such that for any  $\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{2n}$
$(\Phi\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})\left(\hat{D}_{A}(\mathbf{x})\,\hat{\rho}_{AM}\,{\hat{D}_{A}(\mathbf{x})}^{\dagger}\right)=\hat{D}_{B}(K\mathbf{x})\,(\Phi\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})\,{\hat{D}_{B}(K\mathbf{x})}^{\dagger}\;.$
(85)
Let  $\hat{\rho}_{A}$  be the marginal of  $\hat{\rho}_{AM}$  on  $A$ .
Since the quantum conditional mutual information is invariant under local unitaries, we can assume that  $\hat{\rho}_{A}$  has zero first moments.
We have
$S(B|M)_{(\Phi\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})}=S\left((\Phi\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})\right)-S(\hat{\rho}_{M})=S\left(\tilde{\Phi}(\hat{\rho}_{A})\right)-S(\hat{\rho}_{A})\;,$
(86)
where  $\hat{\rho}_{M}$  is the marginal state of  $\hat{\rho}_{AM}$ , and  $\tilde{\Phi}$  is the complementary channel of  $\Phi$ .
Let  $\hat{\gamma}_{A}$  be the quantum Gaussian state with the same first and second moments as  $\hat{\rho}_{A}$ .
Since  $\tilde{\Phi}$  is a Gaussian channel,  $\tilde{\Phi}(\hat{\gamma}_{A})$  is the quantum Gaussian state with the same first and second moments as  $\tilde{\Phi}(\hat{\rho}_{A})$ .
We then have from 8
$\displaystyle S\left(\tilde{\Phi}(\hat{\rho}_{A})\right)-S(\hat{\rho}_{A})$
$\displaystyle=S\left(\tilde{\Phi}(\hat{\gamma}_{A})\right)-S(\hat{\gamma}_{A})+S(\hat{\rho}_{A}\|\hat{\gamma}_{A})-S\left(\left.\tilde{\Phi}(\hat{\rho}_{A})\right\|\tilde{\Phi}(\hat{\gamma}_{A})\right)$
$\displaystyle\geq S\left(\tilde{\Phi}(\hat{\gamma}_{A})\right)-S(\hat{\gamma}_{A})\;,$
(87)
where we have used the data-processing inequality for the quantum relative entropy.
Let  $\alpha$  be the covariance matrix of  $\hat{\gamma}_{A}$ .
We then have
$\hat{\omega}_{A}\left(\|\alpha\|_{\infty}\right)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{2m}}\hat{D}_{A}(\mathbf{x})\,\hat{\gamma}_{A}\,{\hat{D}_{A}(\mathbf{x})}^{\dagger}\,\mathrm{d}p_{X}(\mathbf{x})\;,$
(88)
where  $p_{X}$  is the probability distribution of the classical Gaussian random variable  $X$  with values in  $\mathbb{R}^{2m}$ , zero mean and covariance matrix  $\|\alpha\|_{\infty}I_{2m}-\alpha$ .
We then have from 10
$S\left(\tilde{\Phi}(\hat{\gamma}_{A})\right)-S(\hat{\gamma}_{A})\geq S\left(\tilde{\Phi}\left(\hat{\omega}_{A}\left(\|\alpha\|_{\infty}\right)\right)\right)-S\left(\hat{\omega}_{A}\left(\|\alpha\|_{\infty}\right)\right)\;.$
(89)
10also implies that the function
$\nu\mapsto S\left(\tilde{\Phi}\left(\hat{\omega}_{A}(\nu)\right)\right)-S\left(\hat{\omega}_{A}(\nu)\right)\;,\qquad\nu\geq\frac{1}{2}$
(90)
is decreasing, hence
$\displaystyle S\left(\tilde{\Phi}\left(\hat{\omega}_{A}\left(\|\alpha\|_{\infty}\right)\right)\right)-S\left(\hat{\omega}_{A}\left(\|\alpha\|_{\infty}\right)\right)\geq\lim_{\nu\to\infty}\left(S\left(\tilde{\Phi}\left(\hat{\omega}_{A}(\nu)\right)\right)-S\left(\hat{\omega}_{A}(\nu)\right)\right)$
$\displaystyle=\lim_{\nu\to\infty}\left(S\left((\Phi\otimes\mathbb{I}_{A^{\prime}})(\hat{\omega}_{AA^{\prime}}(\nu))\right)-S\left(\hat{\omega}_{A^{\prime}}(\nu)\right)\right)=\lim_{\nu\to\infty}S(B|A^{\prime})_{(\Phi\otimes\mathbb{I}_{A^{\prime}})(\hat{\omega}_{AA^{\prime}}(\nu))}\;.$
(91)
Lemma 7
For any  $t>0$ ,
$\lim_{\nu\to\infty}S(A|A^{\prime})_{(\mathcal{N}(t)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{A^{\prime}})(\hat{\omega}_{AA^{\prime}}(\nu))}=n\ln t+n\;.$
(92)
Proof
For any  $\nu\geq\frac{1}{2}$ , the quantum Gaussian state  $\hat{\omega}_{AA^{\prime}}(\nu)$  is the tensor product of  $n$  identical two-mode squeezed quantum Gaussian states, each with covariance matrix
$\alpha(\nu):=\left(\begin{array}[]{cc|cc}\nu&0&\sqrt{\nu^{2}-\frac{1}{4}}&0\\
0&\nu&0&-\sqrt{\nu^{2}-\frac{1}{4}}\\
\hline\cr\sqrt{\nu^{2}-\frac{1}{4}}&0&\nu&0\\
0&-\sqrt{\nu^{2}-\frac{1}{4}}&0&\nu\\
\end{array}\right)\;,$
(93)
where the block decomposition refers to the  $AA^{\prime}$  bipartition.
For any  $t\geq 0$ , the quantum Gaussian state  $(\mathcal{N}(t)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{A^{\prime}})(\hat{\omega}_{AA^{\prime}}(\nu))$  is the tensor product of  $n$  identical two-mode quantum Gaussian states, each with covariance matrix
$\alpha(\nu,t):=\left(\begin{array}[]{cc|cc}\nu+t&0&\sqrt{\nu^{2}-\frac{1}{4}}&0\\
0&\nu+t&0&-\sqrt{\nu^{2}-\frac{1}{4}}\\
\hline\cr\sqrt{\nu^{2}-\frac{1}{4}}&0&\nu&0\\
0&-\sqrt{\nu^{2}-\frac{1}{4}}&0&\nu\\
\end{array}\right)\;.$
(94)
The symplectic eigenvalues of  $\alpha(\nu,t)$  are
$\nu_{\pm}(\nu,t)=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{4\nu\,t\pm 2t\sqrt{4\nu\,t+t^{2}+1}+2t^{2}+1}=\sqrt{\nu\,t}+\mathcal{O}(1)$
(95)
for  $\nu\to\infty$ , hence
$\displaystyle\lim_{\nu\to\infty}S(A|A^{\prime})_{(\mathcal{N}(t)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{A^{\prime}})(\hat{\omega}_{AA^{\prime}}(\nu))}$
$\displaystyle=\lim_{\nu\to\infty}n\left(g\left(\nu_{+}(\nu,t)-\frac{1}{2}\right)+g\left(\nu_{-}(\nu,t)-\frac{1}{2}\right)-g\left(\nu-\frac{1}{2}\right)\right)$
$\displaystyle=n\ln t+n\;,$
(96)
where we used that for  $\nu\to\infty$
$g\left(\nu-\frac{1}{2}\right)=\ln\nu+1+\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{1}{\nu^{2}}\right)\;.$
(97)
Theorem 5.2 (universal asymptotic scaling of quantum conditional entropy)
Let  $A$  be a Gaussian quantum system with  $n$  modes, and  $M$  a quantum system.
Let  $\hat{\rho}_{AM}$  be a quantum state on  $AM$  such that its marginal on  $A$  has finite first and second moments, and its marginal on  $M$  has finite entropy.
Then,
$\lim_{t\to\infty}\left(S(A|M)_{(\mathcal{N}(t)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})}-n\ln t-n\right)=0\;.$
(98)
Remark 6
The scaling (98) had been proven in [18], Lemma 6.1 in the particular case where  $\hat{\rho}_{AM}$  is a Gaussian state.
Proof
From the subadditivity of the quantum entropy we have for any  $t\geq 0$
$S(A|M)_{(\mathcal{N}(t)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})}\leq S\left(\mathcal{N}(t)(\hat{\rho}_{A})\right)\;.$
(99)
Let
$E:=\frac{1}{n}\mathrm{Tr}_{A}\left[\hat{H}_{A}\,\hat{\rho}_{A}\right]$
(100)
be the average energy per mode of  $\hat{\rho}_{A}$ , and let  $\hat{\omega}_{A}$  be the thermal quantum Gaussian state with average energy per mode  $E$  and covariance matrix  $\left(E+\frac{1}{2}\right)I_{2n}$ .
For any  $t\geq 0$ ,  $\mathcal{N}(t)(\hat{\omega}_{A})$  is the thermal quantum Gaussian state with the same average energy as  $\mathcal{N}(t)(\hat{\rho}_{A})$ .
We then have from 9
$S\left(\mathcal{N}(t)(\hat{\rho}_{A})\right)\leq S\left(\mathcal{N}(t)(\hat{\omega}_{A})\right)=n\,g(E+t)\;,$
(101)
hence
$\displaystyle\limsup_{t\to\infty}\left(S(A|M)_{(\mathcal{N}(t)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})}-n\ln t-n\right)$
$\displaystyle\leq\limsup_{t\to\infty}n\left(g(E+t)-\ln t-1\right)$
$\displaystyle=0\;.$
(102)
On the other hand, from Theorem 5.1 and 7 we have for any  $t\geq 0$
$S(A|M)_{(\mathcal{N}(t)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})}\geq\lim_{\nu\to\infty}S(A|A^{\prime})_{(\mathcal{N}(t)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{A^{\prime}})(\hat{\omega}_{AA^{\prime}}(\nu))}=n\ln t+n\;.$
(103)
6 Quantum conditional Entropy Power Inequality
In this Section we prove the conditional Entropy Power Inequality, the main result of this paper.
Theorem 6.1 (quantum conditional Entropy Power Inequality)
Let  $A$ ,  $B$  and  $C$  be Gaussian quantum systems with  $n$  modes,  $M$  a quantum system, and  $\mathcal{B}_{\eta}:AB\to C$  the beam-splitter with transmissivity  $0\leq\eta\leq 1$  or the squeezer of parameter  $\eta\geq 1$ .
Let  $\hat{\rho}_{ABM}$  be a quantum state on  $ABM$  such that
$\mathrm{Tr}_{AB}\left[\left(\hat{H}_{A}+\hat{H}_{B}\right)\hat{\rho}_{AB}\right]<\infty\;,\qquad S(\hat{\rho}_{M})<\infty\;,$
(104)
and let us suppose that  $A$  and  $B$  are conditionally independent given  $M$ :
$I(A:B|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{ABM}}=0\;.$
(105)
Then, for any  $0\leq\lambda\leq 1$  the quantum linear conditional Entropy Power Inequality holds:
$\displaystyle\frac{S(C|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{CM}}}{n}$
$\displaystyle\geq\lambda\,\frac{S(A|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{AM}}}{n}+\left(1-\lambda\right)\frac{S(B|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{BM}}}{n}$
$\displaystyle\phantom{\geq}+\lambda\ln\frac{\eta}{\lambda}+(1-\lambda)\ln\frac{|1-\eta|}{1-\lambda}\;.$
(106)
The quantum conditional Entropy Power Inequality follows maximizing over  $\lambda$  the right-hand side of (106):
$\exp\frac{S(C|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{CM}}}{n}\geq\eta\,\exp\frac{S(A|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{AM}}}{n}+\left|1-\eta\right|\exp\frac{S(B|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{BM}}}{n}\;.$
(107)
Remark 7
The quantum linear inequality (106) had been proven for  $\lambda=\eta$  in the special case where  $\hat{\rho}_{ABM}$  is a quantum Gaussian state in [18], Theorem 8.1.
Proof
Let us define for any  $t\geq 0$
$\displaystyle\hat{\rho}_{ABM}(t)$
$\displaystyle:=\left(\mathcal{N}_{A}\left(\frac{\lambda\,t}{\eta}\right)\otimes\mathcal{N}_{B}\left(\frac{(1-\lambda)\,t}{|1-\eta|}\right)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M}\right)(\hat{\rho}_{ABM})\;,$
$\displaystyle\hat{\rho}_{CM}(t)$
$\displaystyle:=(\mathcal{B}_{\eta}\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{ABM}(t))\;.$
(108)
We have for any  $t\geq 0$
$\displaystyle\hat{\rho}_{AM}(t)$
$\displaystyle=\left(\mathcal{N}_{A}\left(\frac{\lambda\,t}{\eta}\right)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M}\right)(\hat{\rho}_{AM})\;,$
(109a)
$\displaystyle\hat{\rho}_{BM}(t)$
$\displaystyle=\left(\mathcal{N}_{B}\left(\frac{(1-\lambda)\,t}{|1-\eta|}\right)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M}\right)(\hat{\rho}_{BM})\;,$
(109b)
$\displaystyle\hat{\rho}_{CM}(t)$
$\displaystyle=\left(\mathcal{N}_{C}(t)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M}\right)(\hat{\rho}_{CM})\;,$
(109c)
where we have set  $\hat{\rho}_{CM}:=\hat{\rho}_{CM}(0)$ .
The time evolution preserves the condition  $I(A:B|M)=0$ .
Indeed, we have from the data-processing inequality for the quantum mutual information
$0\leq I(A:B|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{ABM}(t)}\leq I(A:B|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{ABM}}=0\;.$
(110)
We define the function
$\phi(t):=S(C|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{CM}(t)}-\lambda\,S(A|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{AM}(t)}-(1-\lambda)\,S(B|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{BM}(t)}\;.$
(111)
We have from 1 and Theorem 4.1
$\phi^{\prime}(t)=J(C|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{CM}(t)}-\frac{\lambda^{2}}{\eta}J(A|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{AM}(t)}-\frac{(1-\lambda)^{2}}{|1-\eta|}J(B|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{BM}(t)}\leq 0\;.$
(112)
From Theorem 3.2,  $\phi$  is a linear combination of continuous concave functions, hence it is almost everywhere differentiable and for any  $t\geq 0$
$\phi(t)-\phi(0)=\int_{0}^{t}\phi^{\prime}(s)\,\mathrm{d}s\leq 0\;.$
(113)
We then have from Theorem 5.2
$\displaystyle\phi(0)$
$\displaystyle\geq\lim_{t\to\infty}\phi(t)$
$\displaystyle=\lim_{t\to\infty}\left(S(C|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{CM}(t)}-\lambda\,S(A|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{AM}(t)}-(1-\lambda)\,S(B|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{BM}(t)}\right)$
$\displaystyle=n\left(\lambda\ln\frac{\eta}{\lambda}+\left(1-\lambda\right)\ln\frac{|1-\eta|}{1-\lambda}\right)\;,$
(114)
and the quantum linear conditional Entropy Power Inequality (106) follows.
The quantum conditional Entropy Power Inequality (107) follows choosing
$\lambda=\frac{\eta\,\exp\frac{S(A|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{AM}(t)}}{n}}{\eta\,\exp\frac{S(A|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{AM}(t)}}{n}+\left|1-\eta\right|\exp\frac{S(B|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{BM}(t)}}{n}}\;,$
(115)
that maximizes the right-hand side of (106).
7 Optimality of the quantum conditional Entropy Power Inequality
In this Section, we prove that the quantum conditional Entropy Power Inequality is asymptotically saturated by a suitable sequence of quantum Gaussian input states.
Theorem 7.1 (optimality of the quantum conditional Entropy Power Inequality)
The quantum conditional Entropy Power Inequality (107) is optimal.
In other words, for any  $a,\,b\in\mathbb{R}$  there exists a sequence of quantum Gaussian input states  $\left\{\hat{\gamma}_{ABA^{\prime}B^{\prime}}^{(n)}\right\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$  of the form
$\hat{\gamma}_{ABA^{\prime}B^{\prime}}^{(n)}=\hat{\gamma}_{AA^{\prime}}^{(n)}\otimes\hat{\gamma}_{BB^{\prime}}^{(n)}\;,\qquad n\in\mathbb{N}\;,$
(116)
such that
$\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\exp\left(S(A|A^{\prime}B^{\prime})_{\hat{\gamma}_{AA^{\prime}B^{\prime}}^{(n)}}-1\right)$
$\displaystyle=a\;,$
(117a)
$\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\exp\left(S(B|A^{\prime}B^{\prime})_{\hat{\gamma}_{BA^{\prime}B^{\prime}}^{(n)}}-1\right)$
$\displaystyle=b$
(117b)
and
$\lim_{n\to\infty}\exp\left(S(C|A^{\prime}B^{\prime})_{\hat{\gamma}_{CA^{\prime}B^{\prime}}^{(n)}}-1\right)=\eta\,a+\left|1-\eta\right|b\;,$
(118)
where
$\hat{\gamma}_{CA^{\prime}B^{\prime}}^{(n)}:=\left(\mathcal{B}_{\eta}\otimes\mathbb{I}_{A^{\prime}B^{\prime}}\right)\left(\hat{\gamma}_{AA^{\prime}}^{(n)}\otimes\hat{\gamma}_{BB^{\prime}}^{(n)}\right)\;,$
(119)
and  $A$ ,  $A^{\prime}$ ,  $B$ ,  $B^{\prime}$  and  $C$  are one-mode Gaussian quantum systems.
Proof

Then
$S(\hat{\gamma})=S(\hat{\rho})+S(\hat{\rho}\|\hat{\gamma})\;.$
(144)
Lemma 9
Let  $\hat{\rho}$  be a quantum state on a Gaussian quantum system with finite average energy, and let  $\hat{\omega}$  be the thermal Gaussian quantum state with the same average energy.
Then
$S(\hat{\omega})\geq S(\hat{\rho})\;.$
(145)
Proof
Let  $\beta>0$  be such that
$\hat{\omega}=\frac{\mathrm{e}^{-\beta\hat{H}}}{\mathrm{Tr}\,\mathrm{e}^{-\beta\hat{H}}}\;.$
(146)
We then have
$S(\hat{\omega})=S(\hat{\rho})+S(\hat{\rho}\|\hat{\omega})+\beta\,\mathrm{Tr}\left[\hat{H}\left(\hat{\omega}-\hat{\rho}\right)\right]\geq S(\hat{\rho})\;.$
(147)
Lemma 10
Let  $A$  and  $B$  be Gaussian quantum systems with  $m$  and  $n$  modes, respectively, and  $\Phi:A\to B$  a Gaussian quantum channel.
Let  $\hat{\rho}_{A}$  be a quantum state on  $A$ , and  $p_{X}$  a probability measure on  $\mathbb{R}^{2m}$ .
We define
$\hat{\sigma}_{A}:=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{2m}}\hat{D}_{A}(\mathbf{x})\,\hat{\rho}_{A}\,{\hat{D}_{A}(\mathbf{x})}^{\dagger}\,\mathrm{d}p_{X}(\mathbf{x})\;.$
(148)
Then,
$S(\Phi(\hat{\rho}_{A}))-S(\hat{\rho}_{A})\geq S(\Phi(\hat{\sigma}_{A}))-S(\hat{\sigma}_{A})\;.$
(149)
Proof
Let  $\hat{\sigma}_{AX}$  be the joint state on  $AX$  such that its marginal on  $X$  is  $p_{X}$ , and for any  $\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{2m}$
$\hat{\sigma}_{A|X=\mathbf{x}}=\hat{D}_{A}(\mathbf{x})\,\hat{\rho}_{A}\,{\hat{D}_{A}(\mathbf{x})}^{\dagger}\;.$
(150)
We notice that the marginal of  $\hat{\sigma}_{AX}$  on  $A$  is  $\hat{\sigma}_{A}$ , and
$\displaystyle S(A|X)_{\hat{\sigma}_{AX}}$
$\displaystyle=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{2m}}S\left(\hat{\sigma}_{A|X=\mathbf{x}}\right)\mathrm{d}p_{X}(\mathbf{x})=S(\hat{\rho}_{A})\;,$
(151)
$\displaystyle S(B|X)_{(\Phi\otimes\mathbb{I}_{X})(\hat{\sigma}_{AX})}$
$\displaystyle=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{2m}}S\left(\Phi(\hat{\sigma}_{A|X=\mathbf{x}})\right)\mathrm{d}p_{X}(\mathbf{x})=S(\Phi(\hat{\rho}_{A}))\;,$
(152)
where in the last step we used that for any  $\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{2m}$
$\Phi\left(\hat{D}_{A}(\mathbf{x})\,\hat{\rho}_{A}\,{\hat{D}_{A}(\mathbf{x})}^{\dagger}\right)=\hat{D}_{B}(K\mathbf{x})\,\Phi(\hat{\rho}_{A})\,{\hat{D}_{B}(K\mathbf{x})}^{\dagger}$
(153)
for some matrix  $K:\mathbb{R}^{2m}\to\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ .
We then have
$\displaystyle S(\hat{\sigma}_{A})-S(\hat{\rho}_{A})$
$\displaystyle=I(A:X)_{\hat{\sigma}_{AX}}\;,$
(154)
$\displaystyle S(\Phi(\hat{\sigma}_{A}))-S(\Phi(\hat{\rho}_{A}))$
$\displaystyle=I(B:X)_{(\Phi\otimes\mathbb{I}_{X})(\hat{\sigma}_{AX})}\;,$
(155)
and the claim follows from the data-processing inequality for the mutual information.

Abstract:The bosonic quantum entropy power inequality bounds the entropy of a beam-splitter output in terms of the input entropies. We determine its complete equality class among independent inputs of finite mean photon number: for any number of modes and any transmissivity strictly between zero and one, equality in either the linear or the exponential form holds if and only if the inputs are Gaussian with the same covariance matrix, allowing arbitrary displacements. The main step shows that equality for one output forces the two outputs to be independent: a thermal auxiliary converts equality into preservation of mutual information by a fixed noisy channel, and a two-outcome instrument shows that preservation of mutual information requires a product state with the reference. The quantum Darmois--Skitovich theorem then gives Gaussianity, while a central-limit argument reduces exponential equality to linear equality.

View PDF

Abstract:The classical capacity of a quantum channel generally requires regularization because input codewords may be entangled across channel uses. We remove this regularization for generalized amplitude-damping channels (GADCs) and determine their exact strong-converse exponent throughout the full parameter range. The exponent is a single-letter transform of the sandwiched Rényi Holevo information and is attained by product input codewords with collective decoding. The key ingredient is a decomposition of the joint output into positive operators whose triangular factors have identical scalar Gram matrices after norm compression. A sharp triangular Schatten-norm compression inequality then establishes maximum output norm multiplicativity for diagonally sandwiched GADCs tensored with arbitrary completely positive maps. This yields additivity of the sandwiched Rényi Holevo information at every order above one. Consequently, the classical capacity equals the known one-copy Holevo information and admits a scalar optimization. Thus, entangled input codewords improve neither the capacity nor the optimal exponential decay of decoding success above capacity.

Title:A stable quantum Darmois-Skitovich theorem
Authors:Javier Cuesta

Abstract:The Darmois-Skitovich theorem is a simple characterization of the normal distribution in terms of the independence of linear forms. We present here a non-commutative version of this theorem in the context of Gaussian bosonic states and show that this theorem is stable under small errors in its underlying conditions. An explicit estimate of the stability constants which depend on the physical parameters of the problem is given.
